analysis:
I examined both changed files. No supported security regression was identified.

1) ProviderLoop+Serve.swift head 486: shutdown now also cancels and awaits the selected-model recovery task, alongside the other preload tasks. This tightens lifecycle teardown, so a recovery load cannot outlive shutdown.

2) ProviderLoop+Serve.swift head 512: the inline unload loop over modelSlots/modelsUnloading was replaced by unloadAllModelsForShutdown(). Its body is not in the supplied evidence. It should preserve the old semantics: wait for in-progress unloads and loop until modelSlots is empty. That affects T-028 residual GPU state and availability (T-029), not authorization.

3) ProviderLoop+StartupPreload.swift head 299-305: after the startup preload finishes, candidates that were skipped for insufficient memory or not attempted are queued for SelectedModelRecovery (ProviderLoop+SelectedModelRecovery, not supplied). The queue excludes failed, selfTestFailed and retired models, so fail-closed retirement (retireModelAfterFailedSelfTest, failedSelfTestHashes, isRefusedByRetirement at base 393-474) is not directly bypassed.

The guard checks Task.isCancelled, isShuttingDown and startupPreloadStopRequested, but not servingDrain.refusing. A drain could therefore enqueue a recovery attempt; shutdown cancels it at Serve line 486. This is an availability nuance only.

Integration questions (coverage limits, not findings):
- Recovery loads should go through ensureModelLoaded with verified weight-hash binding (T-012, T-027).
- Recovery must not re-advertise models retired or refused by isRefusedByRetirement, nor add models outside advertisedModels.
- unloadAllModelsForShutdown must fully drain slots.

The unchanged registration attestation, the App Attest resume responder (Serve 205-213) and connection-control handling (401-430) are untouched by this PR. They relate to TB-011/T-053 and show no diff here.
